How much is there to do at the Grand Canyon?
My wife and I did that about 12 years ago. That was a lot of fun.
it's a beautiful ride on a nice animal. one of a kind

If you don't want to hike, I recommend taking a helicopter ride. Trust me the rides are amazing.

Also you may want to go there at the middle of the night; the lack of light pollution offers a spectacular view of the constellations over the Grand Canyon.
I've heard falling for long distances can be fun .

I don't know if you'd be going to the North rim or South rim but both offer great views.

There are a pretty decent number of things to do. I can only speak for the south side because I've only been there though.

As another has said, helicopter rides would be great. I think there are also Pink Jeep tours so you can go off-roading with a driver and a group of other people. The entire south rim has a bus system that is free to use so you can explore different areas of the canyon. There are a number of tourist shops, a few stores and whatnot, I believe inns as well. Further, many people will walk the rim to some degree and stop at signs along the way that explain scientific facts or other random statistics. Some buildings are setup as museums to get more perspective to the canyon, a supported view on a scenic outpoint, and of course to give you ideas about what else you can do there.

There's a lot more I haven't covered though. You kinda just have to go and explore for a while. It will take literally the entire day multiple times over to explore everything.
There's a glass bridge you can walk across at the Grand Canyon. More details inside this link: Trigger warning: Native American flute

There are a number of things you can do. You want to keep in mind that the Grand Canyon is very large and has multiple points of interest that are not nearby each other, e.g. north rim, south rim, various photo-op spots along the Colorado.
